name: bash -i
detail: The `-i` flag forces Bash to run in interactive mode. This ensures that the shell provides a prompt and allows for job control, making it behave like a real terminal session rather than just a one-off command execution.

name: >& (Redirection)
detail: The `>&` operator is a shorthand in Bash that redirects both Standard Output (stdout/1) and Standard Error (stderr/2) to the same destination. This ensures that whether a command succeeds or fails, you see the result on your listener terminal.

name: /dev/tcp/IP/PORT
detail: This is a special feature of Bash. When Bash is compiled with net-redirections enabled, it treats `/dev/tcp/host/port` as a network socket. It opens a connection to your Kali IP and Port, acting as the communication bridge.

desc: Links input to the output stream
detail: This takes Standard Input (stdin/0) and redirects it to Standard Output (1), which is already connected to the network socket. This completes the bidirectional loop: commands go in, and results come out.

name: File Descriptors (0, 1, 2)
detail: The shell relies on the three standard Linux streams: 0 (Input), 1 (Output), and 2 (Error). By mapping all three to the /dev/tcp device, the entire terminal experience is 'piped' over the network connection.
